title: Introduce cost reconciler and rollback automation for quant profile drift
author: Asha Menon
release_notes:
- Add a reconciliation service that replays sampled historical traffic to validate quant profile changes and compute unit-econ deltas.
- Add automated rollback proposals + optional auto-apply opt-in for low-risk tenants.
- New telemetry and dashboards for cost drift, reconciliation outcomes, and rollback rate.
- CLI and runbook for operators to run manual reconciliation and inspect suggested rollbacks.
description:
Context: Quant profile rollouts can produce subtle cost regressions when distribution shifts; we need a way to retroactively validate candidate quant/packing profiles against recent traffic and surface safe rollbacks automatically. This PR introduces a 'cost reconciler' service that replays sampled historical requests (tenant-scoped) through proposed quant profiles to estimate token-level cost deltas and execution latency distributions, then generates rollback proposals when regressions exceed configurable thresholds.

What this PR does (high-level): Implements a reconciliation engine and related operator surface: 1) reconciliation worker that pulls recent request samples from the tenant replay store and runs them through a candidate profile sandbox; 2) scoring and delta model to compute unit-econ impact (tokens, GPU-time, p99 latency); 3) proposal generator that records suggested rollback actions with reason, severity, and suggested operator action; 4) safe-auto-apply path that can be enabled per-tenant for low-severity regressions and only after a manual verification window; 5) CLI commands and console pages to inspect proposals, trigger replays, and force-apply or dismiss proposals.

Why: We've had multiple incidents where quant rollouts increased costs for edge tenants due to unexpected batch-shape changes. This automated, replay-driven reconciliation reduces blast radius by catching regressions before broad rollout. It also provides an auditable trail for finance and SRE.

Changes included (single-line checklist): - add reconciliation service and worker loop - add reconciliation DB schema and migration - add replay sandbox harness (non-prod inference path) - add proposal model and CLI endpoints - add metrics (cost_drift, reconcile_duration, rollback_proposals_created) - dashboard and alert wiring - e2e tests for replay and proposal lifecycle - docs/runbook for operators

Operational notes: The reconciler runs on a configurable cadence (default: daily), samples N requests per tenant (default: 200), and has a soft timeout for long-running sandboxes. It emits events to tracing and creates rollback proposals in the database. Auto-apply is gated: only tenants that have opted in and only for regressions below 5% unit-econ increase and with p99 latency within SLOs.

Security & data handling: Replay uses redacted request payloads by default; full payload replay is available only in VPC/private mode with explicit customer consent (flagged in tenant metadata). All proposals are stamped with a replay_id and operator who approved/merged the candidate profiles.

Related linear/jira: ENG-4982 (reconciler core), ENG-5011 (proposal UI), SUP-3214 (support ticket that motivated safe-auto-apply).

notes_for_ops: Run docs/runbooks/reconciler.md after deploy. Default cadence can be tuned in operator-config under reconciler.cadence. Monitor metrics: reconciler.cost_drift and reconciler.rollback_proposals_created. For immediate manual replay: redwoodctl reconcile run --tenant TENANT_ID --sample 500. Auto-apply opt-in is tenant metadata flag: auto_apply_reconciler=true.
